text.p: London-based broker Actinvest said it was maintaining its buy stance on Italian financial holding company Compart after it sold its Italian concrete group Calcestruzzi late last week.

Activest said in a note on Thursday that Compart's shares were at a discount to their net asset value, and put a price objective of 931 lire on the shares, thus giving a potential increase of over 13 percent.

Compart shares closed on Wednesday at 821.6 lire and today rose 5.15 percent to 864 lire by 1110 GMT reflecting a study again by Actinvest on Wednesday which pointed out that Compart could rejoin the Milan's blue chip MIB 30 index in March at the index's next revision, at the expense of Mediolanum.
Compart, formely Ferruzzi Finanziaria, said it had benefitted around 500 billion lire in cash and transferred debt by selling Calcestruzzi to Italcement in a deal announced on February 14.
